source: Kothari & O'Donnell, Mean estimation when you have the source code; or, quantum Monte Carlo methods (SODA 2023)
theorem: Thm 1.1 (main), Thm 1.3/3.19 (Grover-with-complex-phases distinguisher), Thm 3.18 + Cor 3.23 (eigenvalue constants), Sec 4 eq. (70)-(72) (adaptive stage schedule)
cost_unit: uses of 'the code' for y (synthesizer and its inverse plus a controlled rotation), counted only up to O(.); median of O(log 1/delta) repetitions for delta < 1/3
note: Thm 1.1: O(n) uses give |mu_hat - mu| <= sigma/n with prob >= 2/3; sigma-normalised (so for a Bernoulli amplitude it is relative to sqrt(a(1-a)) <= 1/2), worst case over all distributions. Only intermediate eigenvalue facts have explicit numbers (Cor 3.23: s0=1/16, c0=4/5, C0=5/4, failure 2/9; or the cruder eq. (35)); the final algorithm chains stages with geometric ratio R and failure budgets exp(-C(R)(...)^{1/2}) where C(R) is 'a certain constant' left unspecified, and the total cost is only given as O(1/eps). No end-to-end numerical c(delta) can be evaluated without redoing the analysis; and even then the multi-stage + phase-estimation structure would very likely give a constant well above canonical BHMT.
label: lit

theorem: Thm 4.2 (sub-Gaussian estimator), Prop 4.1 (Bernoulli estimator), Thm A.3 (BHMT restated), Thm A.4 (sequential AE)
c_delta_0003: Main Thm 4.2: not computable (hidden constant d and O(n log^{3/2} n log log n) cost). Prop 4.1 construction, if read as plain BHMT + median: 6*log(1/delta) copies of AEst at M ~ 2n/log(1/delta); at delta=0.003 with natural log, 6*ln(333.3)=6*5.81=34.9 -> 35 copies; worst case a=1/2 needs M ~ pi/eps per copy (BHMT Thm 12: pi/M + pi^2/M^2 <= eps), so c ~ 35*pi ~ 110 (about 158 if log is base 2).
cost_unit: 'quantum experiments' = applications of U, U^dagger and the reflection I-2Pi (Thm A.3); Prop 4.1 count includes the median repetitions; Thm 4.2 counted only up to O(.)
verdict: not explicit (main theorem); Prop 4.1 is just canonical BHMT + a loose Chernoff median count, i.e. explicit-but-worse-than-canonical
note: Thm 4.2: with O(n log^{3/2}(n) log log(n)) experiments, |mu_hat - mu| <= sigma*sqrt(log(1/delta))/n with prob >= 1-delta, under n >= log(1/delta); constants hidden (Algorithm 2 uses 'a constant d > 1 chosen in the proof'). Prop 4.1 error bound is stated as a sqrt(b mu log(1/delta))/n + b log(1/delta)^2/n^2 shape with O(n) cost; the extracted PDF text lost relation symbols, so I could not confirm whether the stated inequality carries explicit leading constants; its proof is BHMT Thm 12 (success 8/pi^2) + median of 6 log(1/delta) runs. Nothing better than canonical BHMT + median.
label: lit

source: Rall, Faster coherent quantum algorithms for phase, energy, and amplitude estimation (Quantum 5, 566 (2021))
theorem: Prop 5 (standard phase estimation + median), Lemma 11 (QSP amplifying polynomial), Thm 12 (coherent iterative PE), Cor 13 (improved PE), Cor 20 (non-destructive AE); Def 1 (rounding promise); Sec 3 (numerical comparison)
worst_case: partial: Thm 12/Prop 5 are stated under an (n,alpha)-rounding promise (eigenphases excluded from an alpha-fraction near bin edges); Cor 13 also covers the no-promise case, outputting floor(2^n phi) or floor(2^n phi)-1, i.e. a +-1-bin guarantee for every phase, up to diamond-norm error delta
non_asymptotic: Prop 5 yes; Thm 12 yes given M; Cor 13 and Cor 20 only O(.)
explicit: Prop 5 yes (closed form); Thm 12 only via M from Lemma 11, which is 'O(Delta^-1 log delta^-1)' and is computed numerically from Low-Chuang App. A ('not worth re-stating'); Cor 13/20 hidden constants
c_delta_0003: Prop 5 only: reps = ceil(ln(1/delta)/(2*eta0^2)) with eta0 = 8/pi^2 - 1/2 = 0.3106, 2*eta0^2 = 0.1929; ln(333.3)=5.809 -> 5.809/0.1929 = 30.1 -> 31 reps of (2^n - 1) queries; with +-1-bin error 2^-n <= eps (phase in turns) c ~ 31 per eps-in-turns; for amplitude a = sin^2(pi*theta), |da| <= pi|dtheta| -> c ~ 31*pi ~ 97. QSP estimators (Thm 12/Cor 13): not computable from the paper's text; constants exist only as numerical plots in Sec 3.
cost_unit: calls to U (or the block-encoding U_H); Cor 20 counts controlled applications of the two reflections R and R_psi; Prop 5 count includes the median repetitions; error measured in diamond norm (failure prob delta)
verdict: Prop 5: explicit-but-worse-than-canonical (it is textbook PE + Hoeffding median, i.e. the canonical construction with a loose repetition count); QSP results: not explicit (numerical only) and stated under a rounding promise
note: Rall's claimed ~14x phase-estimation speed-up is measured against his own Prop 5 textbook baseline in numerical plots, not as a certified closed-form c(delta). No closed-form worst-case coverage constant for the QSP/coherent estimator is given. Diamond-norm delta does translate to a failure probability, so a numerical certificate could in principle be extracted by computing the Low-Chuang polynomial degree M for given (Delta, delta), but the paper does not state one for the no-promise case.
label: lit

source: Kimmel, Low, Yoder, Robust calibration of a universal single-qubit gate set via robust phase estimation (PRA 92, 062315 (2015))
theorem: Thm I.1 (robust PE, O(1/sigma) time), Thm V.1 (from Higgins et al.), eqs. (V.9)-(V.12) (sigma*T < 12.4, or < 10.7), Lemmas A.1-A.2; v3 Errata at top of paper
explicit: yes for the standard-deviation bound (sigma(A_hat)*T < 10.7 at alpha=5/2, beta=1/2), but the erratum (v3, Oct 2021) says the Sec. V A error-event analysis is incorrect (error condition should be pi/(3k_j), not pi/(2k_j)), so the 10.7 constant is not valid as stated; corrected constants are deferred to other works
c_delta_0003: No coverage theorem. Via Chebyshev only (not in the paper): P(|err| > eps) <= sigma^2/eps^2 -> T = 10.7/(sqrt(delta)*eps_rad) = 10.7/0.05477 = 195/eps_rad at delta=0.003 (or about 98/eps for amplitude if eps_A = 2 eps_a); this uses the retracted 10.7 and is far worse than canonical anyway.
cost_unit: 'time' T = sum over experiments of k (applications of the target rotation), both |0> and |+> experiment families; phase A in radians on (-pi, pi]; not controlled-U (single-qubit sequences)
verdict: not worst-case-coverage (RMSE only); explicit constant retracted by erratum; any coverage bound derived from it is far worse than canonical
note: Theorem I.1 is an RMSE/standard-deviation statement with O(.) in the theorem and explicit constants only in Sec. V. A 99% coverage statement with an explicit constant does not follow directly; one could redo the per-stage union bound (P(error at stage j) <= Hoeffding term) to get a coverage bound, but the paper does not state it.
label: lit

source: Belliardo & Giovannetti, Achieving Heisenberg scaling with maximally entangled states: an analytic upper bound for the attainable RMSE (PRA 102, 042613 (2020))
theorem: eqs. (27)-(33) (Hoeffding per-stage error bound and MSE sum), eq. (30) (numerical A=0.5949, C=1.664), eq. (45) (sigma^2 N^2 <= (24.26)^2 at x_K=11); Thm IV.1 concerns limited entanglement size
worst_case: yes in the analytic route (Hoeffding, A=4, C=e^{2 eta^2}=1.206 with eta=sqrt6/8); the 24.26 constant uses A, C fitted by maximising over 100 grid angles, so it is only a numerical worst case
explicit: yes for MSE (24.26 with numerically fitted A,C; the purely analytic A=4, C=1.206 gives a much larger constant that the paper does not evaluate as a headline number)
c_delta_0003: No coverage theorem. Via Chebyshev only (not in the paper): N = 24.26/(sqrt(delta)*eps_rad) = 24.26/0.05477 = 443/eps_rad at delta=0.003 (about 70/eps in turns; about 221/eps for amplitude with eps_phase = 2 eps_a). Far worse than canonical.
cost_unit: number N of probes = total phase imprintings (applications of U, via GHZ states or equivalent multipass); includes the nu_j repetitions per stage; phase in radians
verdict: not worst-case coverage (RMSE only); explicit-but-worse-than-canonical if converted by Chebyshev
note: The paper's per-stage bound P(|phi_hat_j - phi_j| >= pi/3) <= A C^{-nu_j} is exactly the ingredient for a union-bound coverage theorem (P(any stage wrong) <= sum_j A C^{-nu_j}), but the paper does not state a coverage theorem or optimise for it; doing so would be new work and the Hoeffding constants (C=1.206 analytic) are weak.
label: lit

source: Accelerated Quantum Amplitude Estimation without QFT (AQAE), arXiv 2024 (authors not recorded; read via arXiv HTML)
theorem: Thm 2 (Algorithm 1) and Thm 4 (Algorithm 2, accelerated); constants E~0.06937 (eq. 43), F~0.19084 (eq. 45), C=4/(6F+pi) (eq. 13)
c_delta_0003: Thm 2: M < (1/eps)[(1/(4E^2))((3/2)F ln(2/(C alpha F)) + (3/4)F ln3 + (pi/4) ln(8/(C alpha pi))) + (3/4)F + pi/8] ~ (85.637 - 55.674 ln alpha)/eps (my re-derivation from the constants gives 85.64 - 55.67 ln alpha). delta=0.003: ln=-5.809, 55.674*5.809=323.4, c=409.1. delta=0.01: ln=-4.605, 55.674*4.605=256.4, c=342.0. Thm 4 (accelerated, worst case): ~ (101.4 - 61.2 ln alpha)/eps (my arithmetic, C=8/(3pi)) -> c(0.003)=457, c(0.01)=383; worse than Thm 2 in the worst case.
cost_unit: applications of Q summed over all shots (a shot of Q^k A|0> counts k); applications of A and measurement shots not counted separately; controlled-Q not needed (no QFT)
note: Statement: for every a in [0,1], eps>0, P(|a_hat - a| <= eps) >= 1-alpha with at most M Q-applications, M bounded pathwise (not in expectation). The paper's sharper figure E[M] < (27.380 - 10.201 ln alpha)/eps is a computer-assisted expected-cost bound, not a worst-case one (at alpha=0.003 it would be 86.6). Paper also restates IQAE M < (50/eps) ln((1/alpha) log2(pi/(4 eps))) and MIQAE M < (62/eps) ln(6/alpha). Read through the WebFetch HTML summariser, not line-by-line; the constant 85.637 - 55.674 ln alpha was cross-checked by recomputing from E, F, C.
label: lit

source: Manzano, Musso, Leitao, Real Quantum Amplitude Estimation (RQAE)
note: Abstract claims a rigorous performance analysis and a quadratic speed-up 'modulo logarithmic corrections', i.e. its bound carries extra log factors in 1/eps, so it cannot give a pure c(delta)/eps + c0 form; abstract does not mention explicit constants. Theorem not read; do not cite as checked.

source: Labib, Quantum amplitude estimation beyond power-of-two schedules (2 Sept 2026)
note: Non-adaptive MLE estimator with geometric depth ratio ~1.45. Abstract reports measured total query complexity 2.8-3.1/eps at 95% confidence (target errors 3.5e-3 to 1e-6), near-parity with chebAE, and a 1.5-1.7x improvement over csAE at 99%. These are benchmark/empirical constants with an error-probability model that 'reproduces the measured failure rates'; no certified worst-case theorem is claimed in the abstract. Relevant as the strongest recent empirical competitor, not as a certified constant.
label: lit
